title: Bengal's BJP Cabinet Takes Shape With Portfolio Picks
excerpt: Suvendu Adhikari assigns key ministries to five sworn-in ministers, with a cabinet expansion already scheduled for May 18.
body:
Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari formally allocated portfolios to the five cabinet ministers sworn in on May 9, 2026, completing the first structural step of West Bengal's first-ever BJP-led government — a government that arrived with a mandate no one in Delhi or Kolkata expected to be quite this decisive.

**Who got what:**
Dilip Ghosh received Panchayat Affairs and Rural Development along with Animal Husbandry; Agnimitra Paul was given Women and Child Development, Social Welfare, and Municipal Affairs; Ashok Kirtaniya was allotted Food and Supplies; and Khudiram Tudu received Backward Class Welfare and Development. Nisith Pramanik was entrusted with North Bengal Development along with Sports and Youth Welfare. A senior BJP leader said the distribution reflected the party's attempt to balance organisational experience with regional and social representation.

**Why the picks signal intent:**
The 2026 Assembly elections gave the BJP 206 seats in the 294-member House, reducing the Trinamool Congress to 80 seats. At its first cabinet meeting, the new government announced the rollout of Ayushman Bharat, PM Jan Arogya Yojana, PM SHRI, Vishwakarma Scheme, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao, and Ujjwala Yojana — schemes that Bengal had withheld from its citizens under the Mamata Banerjee government for years. The cabinet also decided to transfer land to the BSF for border fencing along Bangladesh and approved immediate implementation of the Census in the state.

**What to watch:**
The next cabinet meeting is scheduled for May 18, with more members expected to be announced — and with the state constitutionally permitted to have as many as 44 ministers, Adhikari has considerable room to reward allies and cement regional coalitions.

nri_angle: For the 500,000-plus Bengali-Americans spread across New York, New Jersey, and Texas, this cabinet formation marks the first time in their lifetimes that a BJP government controls the state that many of their families still call home — reshaping the politics, welfare access, and economic trajectory of the region in ways that will ripple across diaspora ties and remittances.
